newsitem.title: USA: Columbia/HCA discusses merger with Tenet-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Columbia/HCA discusses merger with Tenet-WSJ.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Corp, in the midst of a growing federal Medicare fraud inquiry, is holding discussions with rival Tenet HealthCare about a possible combination, the Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday.
Citing people familiar with the situation, the paper said that the talks could collapse at any time and no merger was imminent. Neither company would comment.
Hospital market leader Columbia/HCA has a market value of about $21.5 billion while Tenet, which is number two, is valued at about $8.3 billion.
Meanwhile, the Columbia probe by Federal authorities is examining whether the company billed Medicare for specific kinds of blood tests that physicians didn't request or use, the paper said.
